facts.statement: The only known fossil of Pneumatoraptor is a single complete left shoulder girdle discovered in the Csehbánya Formation of western Hungary.
facts.quote: It is known from a single complete left shoulder girdle (scapulocoracoid) found in the Csehbánya Formation of the Iharkút locality in the Bakony Mountains of western Hungary.

facts.statement: The species was named Pneumatoraptor fodori in honor of Géza Fodor, who funded the excavation.
facts.quote: The type species is Pneumatoraptor fodori, named for Géza Fodor, who provided funding for the dig.

facts.statement: The genus name means "air thief" because the bones contained hollow spaces filled with air sacs.
facts.quote: The genus name Pneumatoraptor, which means "air thief", refers to the pneumaticity of the bone, the hollow spaces that would have been filled with air sacs in life.

facts.statement: The animal was approximately three times smaller than Velociraptor based on the size of its shoulder bone.
facts.quote: The bone is small, indicating that the animal was about three times smaller than Velociraptor.

facts.statement: Its L-shaped shoulder girdle identifies it as a member of the Paraves group, which includes dromaeosaurids, troodontids, and birds.
facts.quote: The shoulder girdle is L-shaped, showing it to be a member of the group Paraves, which also includes the dromaeosaurids, troodontids, and birds.

facts.statement: Although the remains are too incomplete to definitively place it in a specific subgroup, many bone features are similar to dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: While the Pneumatoraptor remains are too incomplete to tell which, if any, of these specific groups it belongs to, many of the features of the bones are similar to dromaeosaurids.

facts.statement: Pneumatoraptor lived during the Santonian age of the late Cretaceous period, approximately 85 million years ago.
facts.quote: This formation dates to the late Cretaceous period (Santonian age) about 85 million years ago.

facts.statement: Pneumatoraptor is classified as a small paravian dinosaur, possibly belonging to the dromaeosaurid family.
facts.quote: Pneumatoraptor is a genus of small paravian, possibly a dromaeosaurid, dinosaur

facts.statement: The fossil record for Pneumatoraptor spans from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, cataloged as MTM V.2008.38.1, is housed at the Hungarian Natural History Museum in Budapest.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is identified by the catalog number MTM V.2008.38.1. and housed at the Hungarian Natural History Museum in Budapest.

rejected.statement: Pneumatoraptor is distinguished by a narrow shoulder blade that is nearly circular in cross-section and features a large opening for an air sac cavity.
rejected.quote: Pneumatoraptor differs from other theropods in having a narrow shoulder blade that is nearly circular in cross section, as well as having a large opening in the bone to house a hollow air sac cavity.

rejected.statement: Other remains from the same formation, including isolated teeth, claws, tail vertebrae, and a partial tibia, may also belong to Pneumatoraptor.
rejected.quote: Other paravian remains from the same formation may belong to Pneumatoraptor. These include isolated teeth, claws, tail vertebrae, and a partial lower leg bone (tibia).
